note: METHOD (about 70 tool calls, 2 WebSearch). One background script queried all 288 composers: Deezer album search on 'Given Surname' and on the surname (25 results each); MusicBrainz artist search (ten composers per request, matched on name and dates) and, for a matched artist, every work with its linked recordings; and Apple's composerTerm song search for the 252 composers without a Deezer chamber hit (screened by script for chamber-titled tracks that carry the surname or a candidate's opus number, and the chamber-titled collections of the rest read by eye in a compact digest). Hits were opened through Deezer album and Apple lookup track lists, a MusicBrainz release, and IMSLP's api.php. A second Deezer pass ('<Surname> trio / quartet / quintet / chamber') was added because the plain surname search is swamped by namesakes (Parry's Hyperion discs turned up only that way, Lindblad, Popper and Rudorff in the second pass); it ran for all 257 composers whose surname search returned more than 25 albums (for the others the first pass read every result); it also found Lyapunov's sextet. RESULT: 43 composers had a commercial recording in scope: 83 works kept, 27 of them not on IMSLP; 508 candidate pages skipped. The others are 'triage: none found'. NOTHING WAS LEFT UNCHECKED: no page is skipped as 'not checked'; the two composers marked 'partial' are Miles (Apple and MusicBrainz works not read for his ten unrecorded pages) and Levy (the quartet's attribution on the Selo Sesc disc is inferred). WEAK 'none found': initials or a single name only (Loewenthal G., Michel L., Polak-Daniels B., Roux A.B., Saint-Julien H. de) and common surnames (Levy/Lévy, Meyer, Müller, Peters, Neumann, Ritter, Rey, Roux, Richter, Pinto, Perry, Parker, Perkins, Mohr, Reuss, Rousseau, Lorenz). LOW CONFIDENCE (the owner may drop them): Levy's String Quartet (the Selo Sesc disc holds two unlabelled quartets; the first is taken as Levy's from the order of the names); Müller-Hermann's Piano Quintet Op. 31 (scoring inferred from the five players); De Meglio's Andante e allegro Op. 67 (matched to a recorded two-movement G-major trio by its title only); Lindblad's String Quintet (disc says A major, IMSLP F). MEDIUM: Miles (label MPR, professional players, retail listings; ten other Miles pages have IMSLP audio only), Popper (Czech Clarton disc), Noskowski's quartet numbering (two discs list a No. 2 in E and a No. 2 in D), Nepomuceno (disc numbering Nos. 1-3 matched to SN 5.5-5.7), Moniuszko (disc says D major for No. 1, IMSLP D minor), Posa and Rangström (keys left out). SCOPE CALLS. Not entered: Popp's Gesellschafts-Trios Op. 409 (IMSLP scores it flute or violin, harmonium, piano; only Vol. 1, three pieces, is on a harmonium label and the top instrument is not named); Pedrell's Nocturnes Op. 55 (Trio Arbos records a one-movement 'Nocturne-Trio' for piano trio, match to IMSLP's violin-cello-piano-harmonium page unconfirmed); Melcer-Szczawinski's Piano Trio Op. 2 (one 10-minute track on a competition anthology); Moja's Sonata Op. 22 (mandolin-group EP); Oswald's Piano Quartet Op. 26 (2013 release on a label named after the composer, performers not named); Ryelandt's Quartet Op. 13 (one movement, 7 min) and Andante and Variations; O'Neill's 'Pretty Polly Oliver' variations (scoring not confirmed); Rutkowski's string-quartet variations (university press set); Noskowski's Variations on a theme of Viotti and Humorous Quartet.
